title: Redux Small Examples
description: Use these small Redux examples with the tools described in each lesson. Read the expected result before you try a change.

examples.title: Meet a store and an action
examples.description: A store keeps state. An action is a small message saying what happened, such as one more book being read.
examples.output: The console shows 1 after the action is dispatched.

examples.title: Name a slice of state
examples.description: A slice groups one part of state with the reducers that change it.

examples.title: Carry a value in an action
examples.description: An action payload carries the information needed for a change.
examples.output: The store becomes 3 because the action payload is 3.

examples.title: Return a new primitive value
examples.description: When a slice state is a number or string, its reducer returns the next value.
examples.output: The reset reducer returns 0 from a previous state of 7.

examples.title: Update draft object fields
examples.description: Redux Toolkit uses Immer inside createSlice reducers.
examples.output: The output is false true. The original object remains unchanged.

examples.title: Add a list item
examples.description: A list reducer can add a record with a stable id.
examples.output: The new list contains a book titled Moon Trip.

examples.title: Select a useful piece of state
examples.description: A selector is a function that reads state and returns the part a caller needs.
examples.output: The selector finds one unread book.

examples.title: Combine related slices
examples.description: A store can hold several slices under different keys.
examples.output: The root state has books and theme keys. The theme value is light.

examples.title: Provide the store to React
examples.description: React Redux Provider makes one store available to components under it.
examples.output: Components inside App can use React Redux hooks with the supplied store.

examples.title: Read and dispatch from React
examples.description: useSelector reads a store value for a component.
examples.output: The button reads the count and asks the store to add one. Its display follows the updated value.

examples.title: Handle an async task state
examples.description: An async thunk creates pending, fulfilled and rejected actions for a promise.
examples.output: The fulfilled action stores the returned list and the console shows Moon Trip.

examples.title: Keep state changes predictable
examples.description: Reducers should be predictable: the same state and action should produce the same result.
examples.output: The same empty state and action always give a one-item list.
